newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica inflation dips for first time in 11 months.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica inflation dips for first time in 11 months.

text.p: South African inflation dipped for the first time in 11 months in March but economists cautioned that it was likely to kick up again in April before peaking, possibly in May, at around 10 percent.

The Central Statistical Service said on Wednesday that the all-items consumer price index rose 0.6 percent in March from February, taking the year-on-year rate to 9.6 percent versus February's 9.8 percent.
The monthly rise reflected increases in the price indices for food (contributing 0.1 percentage point), housing (0.1), education (0.2) and other items (0.2).

The bond market was unmoved by the better-than-expected figures -- the consensus forecast had been for a 9.7 percent rise -- with players believing the data was unlikely to impact on the interest rate outlook given the Reserve Bank's focus on high bank credit and money supply growth.
March money supply and private sector credit extension data is due on Friday at 1500 GMT.
There were also concerns that April's inflation rate would be lifted again, partly due to increases taxes on tobacco and alcohol introduced in last month's budget.
"I'm still expecting a peak of around 9.9 percent in May," said Tertia Jacobs of SocGen Frankel Pollak.
Sandra Gordon of Syfrets also saw a peak of 9.9 percent, but coming in April rather than May.
However, the slightly lower than expected March rate suggested that worst inflation fears in the wake of last year's sharp fall in the rand could be avoided.
"It now looks like we can avoid double digit inflation," Gordon said.
